default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-798.title: First-window return predicts late-day move
E-798.hypothesis: Intraday momentum: the first-window return of the session pushes institutional rebalancing and late hedging the same way; buy/sell when the last hours begin in the direction of the opening-window move.

E-799.title: Return autocorrelation regime switch
E-799.hypothesis: When the rolling lag-1 autocorrelation of bar returns is strongly positive, a big bar is followed by more flow in its direction; when strongly negative, liquidity providers fade it. Trade the regime.

E-800.title: Heavy-volume small-range absorption at the range edge
E-800.hypothesis: Big volume with a small range at the edge of the recent range means passive orders absorb the aggressors; trade away from the edge.

E-801.title: Day-open recross follow
E-801.hypothesis: The session open is a reference many participants watch; after a long stay on one side, a close back across it flips the day's bias.

E-802.title: Session-record range bar exhaustion fade
E-802.hypothesis: A bar with the widest range of the session that closes at its extreme is a climax where the last aggressors enter; fade it.

E-803.title: Range-edge dwell continuation
E-803.hypothesis: Closes that stay in the top (bottom) fifth of the recent range for a while show persistent one-sided demand; follow when the dwell starts.

E-804.title: Session midrange cross follow
E-804.hypothesis: Once the day has a wide range, the midpoint of high and low is the balance line; a close across it shows control moving to the other side.

E-805.title: EMA stack alignment follow
E-805.hypothesis: When fast, medium and slow EMAs line up in order and price is beyond the fast one, trend followers across horizons agree; enter on the alignment.

E-806.title: Regression t-statistic trend follow
E-806.hypothesis: A statistically strong linear trend over the window (high t-stat of price on time) marks a one-way flow; join when the t-stat first exceeds the bar.

E-807.title: Kaufman efficiency-ratio surge follow
E-807.hypothesis: When price covers a window almost in a straight line (efficiency ratio high), little counter-flow exists; follow the direction on the first crossing.
